headline: AlphaFold-class predictions probed for failure modes in non-globular and fusion proteins
label: Alphafold Limits And Applications
summary: New benchmarks show AlphaFold-type predictions diverge from biological states in non-globular and fusion proteins, while AlphaFold models also enable membrane-protein annotation.
synthesis: The shared thread is a critical assessment of what AlphaFold-class structure predictions represent biologically. One preprint uses experimentally validated non-globular proteins to show where predictions diverge from biologically relevant structural states. A second benchmarks four folding tools on control, cancer-associated and fusion proteins, finding that inter-tool agreement on fusions does not indicate biological plausibility. In contrast, the AlphaPPM pipeline and MembranomeX resource use AlphaFold models constructively, identifying and membrane-orienting bitopic proteins across 18 organisms. Taken together, the items emphasize that model confidence or consensus cannot substitute for biological validation, while showing that model outputs remain useful for proteome-scale annotation when the target class is well defined. The evolutionary-information and interpretability themes in the prior synthesis are not supported by the current items.
